leftEvidence.title: The shepherd lays down his life

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Jesus contrasts the good shepherd with the hired hand, speaks of knowing the sheep, gathering one flock, laying down his life, and taking it again by received command.
points.right: The writer says love is known because Jesus laid down his life, then turns to brothers and sisters, material need, action, truth, and mutual life-giving.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The passage materially bears on the Crucifixion while leaving part of its motive, mechanism, or later significance unstated.
points.right: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.

payload.posture: The shepherd’s voluntary laying down of life is later used as the stated way love becomes known.

rightEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
rightEvidence.title: Love known by a laid-down life

payload.tension: John’s Gospel emphasizes authority, sheep, taking up life, and the Father’s command; the letter turns the laid-down life toward material care for others.
payload.title: Shepherd lays down life / love known
